Autumn colors and Mount Fuji

A quick recap of the [autumn color season](https://www.japan-guide.com/autumn-colors/) so far, we started our [autumn color reporting](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/) at the end of September with [Schauwecker](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/schauwecker/) in [Daisetsuzan](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6775.html) in [Hokkaido](https://www.japan-guide.com/list/e1101.html), and kept to the higher elevations for the first few reports. By now, the peak of the season is over in many places in the northern half of the [Tohoku Region](https://www.japan-guide.com/list/e1102.html), while the southern half is at the peak. The colors have yet to reach the major cities of [Tokyo](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2164.html), [Kyoto](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2158.html) and [Osaka](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2157.html), but it should not be long before city dwellers can appreciate the changing season.

Today I went to the [Fuji Five Lakes](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6900.html) region, specifically to [Lake Kawaguchiko](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6906.html) and [Lake Yamanakako](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6908.html) to see how the [autumn colors](https://www.japan-guide.com/autjmn-colors/) have developed. I arrived to find the colors at both lakes to be very attractive. I expect this weekend and next week to be the best time for viewing autumn colors.

## [Momiji Tunnel](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6906.html)

Approaching Peak

·November 7, 2025

I started my day bright and early at Momiji Tunnel, a small area with many maple trees. The leaves here were the least developed of all the ones I saw today, only around the 50 percent mark. I expect more green leaves to change colors over the next few days, and for the trees to reach their peak colors next week.

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251107_fuji_01.jpg)

Lone photographer and I with Mount Fuji and some great autumn colors

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251107_fuji_13.jpg)

Momiji Tunnel is not as crowded as the bigger areas around Lake Kawaguchiko

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251107_fuji_06.jpg)

Refreshing green leaves

## [Momiji Corridor](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6906.html)

Approaching Peak

·November 7, 2025

A ten minute drive from the Momiji Tunnel brought me the Momiji Corridor, a stretch of maple trees that flank a small canal, near the northern shore of [Lake Kawaguchiko](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6906.html). The exterior of the maple trees were blazing red, but the interior of the corridor were still mostly green. However, I thought the mix of colors made the momiji corridor very attractive, and enjoyed my visit a lot.

A stone's throw from the corridor are the cherry trees along the northern shore - a popular attraction in spring to see cherry blossoms. In the fall, the leaves of the cherry trees also turn copper-red and make for a nice autumn color addition to the maple leaves.

Until November 30, 2025, there is an autumn color festival near the Momiji Corridor. During the festival period, the trees are illuminated until 21:30. Handicraft shops and food vendors set up shop around the entrance of the corridor and along the main street.

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251107_fuji_11.jpg)

Main road near the Momiji Corridor with blazing maple leaves

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251107_fuji_03.jpg)

Momiji Corridor looks very promising from the outside

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251107_fuji_02.jpg)

My expectations were quite high

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251107_fuji_04.jpg)

But it is more green on the inside ^^;

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251107_fuji_05.jpg)

Choice colors

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251107_fuji_07.jpg)

I visited before the shops opened

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251107_fuji_10.jpg)

Walking along the shore where the cherry trees are

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251107_fuji_09.jpg)

Cherry blossoms in spring and autumn colors in fall

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251107_fuji_12.jpg)

Even the parking area looks attractive

## [Panorama Dai](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6908.html)

Peak Color

·November 7, 2025

Next, I headed over to Panorama Dai, an observation deck near [Lake Yamanakako](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6908.html). The observation deck was renewed last year, and now offers visitors a comfortable place to see and appreciate the views. Pampas grass or susuki can be seen around Panorama Dai, and they were at their fluffy autumnal best when I visited. Note that there is limited parking at the observation deck and the road leading there may get congested on the weekends.

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251107_fuji_14.jpg)

Renewed observation deck

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251107_fuji_15.jpg)

Beautiful view of Mount Fuji and Lake Yamanakako. I could even see the southern Alps (to the right of Mount Fuji in this image) today

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251107_fuji_16.jpg)

Fluffy pampas grass

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251107_fuji_17.jpg)

There was a huge line of vehicles waiting for parking, which lead to traffic coming to a standstill

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251107_fuji_18.jpg)

Mountain and grass

## [Yuyake no Nagisa Park](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6908.html)

Peak Color

·November 7, 2025

Finally, I made my way to Yuyake no Nagisa Park along the shore of [Lake Yamanakako](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6908.html). The colors here were at their peak, and I felt like I had saved the best for the last. I recommend those planning a visit to go to the park sooner rather than later so as not to miss the peak of the season.

Until November 16, walking paths and trees in the park are illuminated from 16:30 to 20:30.

## Introduction

Kawaguchiko is a lake that spreads on the north side of Mt. Fuji. Many inns and hotels line up, and it's a popular tourist destination where you can enjoy spectacular views of Mt. Fuji. The area around Kawaguchiko enters the autumn foliage season in November.

The average temperature throughout the day at Kawaguchiko doesn't reach 10℃ (50℉) and is a bit chilly compared to Tokyo, but you can enjoy beautiful autumn foliage in nature. This time, we will introduce recommended autumn foliage spots around Kawaguchiko, focusing on the Kawaguchiko Autumn Festival.

## At Kawaguchiko, the annual "Kawaguchiko Autumn Festival" is held every November

![At Kawaguchiko, the annual "Kawaguchiko Autumn Festival" is held every November](https://res-3.cloudinary.com/dbm1qiew0/image/upload/q_auto/v1/blog-images/kawaguchiko-autumn-festival%40image1--1-.jpg)

At Kawaguchiko, the Kawaguchiko Autumn Festival is held every year during the autumn foliage season. Around Kawaguchiko, there are many spots where you can enjoy autumn foliage along with spectacular views of Mt. Fuji, and the magnificent Mt. Fuji towering in the world dyed in red is one of the sights you should definitely see if you visit Kawaguchiko during this time.

The event is held over a wide area around Kawaguchiko, but at the main venue on the north shore of Kawaguchiko, local gourmet food stalls line up, and you can also enjoy illuminations and handmade markets.

<Information>

Schedule: November 1-30, 2026, 9:00- 17:00 (Illumination until 21:30)

Access: Get off at "Itchiku Kubota Art Museum," 5-minute walk (Main venue)

Admission: Free

## In November, Momiji Road and Momiji Street are beautifully colored

![In November, Momiji Road and Momiji Street are beautifully colored](https://res-3.cloudinary.com/dbm1qiew0/image/upload/q_auto/v1/blog-images/kawaguchiko-autumn-festival%40image1--7-.jpg)

When it comes to highlights of the Kawaguchiko Autumn Festival, there are "Momiji Street" and "Momiji Road." In these two areas located at the main venue of the event, Momiji (Japanese maple) grows densely, creating a beautiful autumn foliage world. If you visit the event, be sure to stop by these two areas.

### What is Momiji Highway?

![What is Momiji Highway?](https://res-4.cloudinary.com/dbm1qiew0/image/upload/q_auto/v1/blog-images/kawaguchiko-autumn-festival%40image1--8-.jpg)

"Momiji Highway" is a 1.2km street that runs along the north shore of Kawaguchiko. Momiji trees are planted along the road, and when the autumn foliage season enters in late October, they turn bright red. The lakeside is wrapped in autumn foliage, and beautiful Mt. Fuji shows its face through the trees.

Usually, it is a modern and calm street lined with art museums, but during the event period, it is bustling with the voices of people enjoying the autumn foliage. During the day, young people enjoy taking photos in the bright atmosphere, and in the evening, couples hold hands in the calm scenery. Illumination is also held at night, and you can enjoy strolling in a romantic atmosphere.

![What is Momiji Road?](https://res-4.cloudinary.com/dbm1qiew0/image/upload/q_auto/v1/blog-images/kawaguchiko-autumn-festival%40image1--4-.jpg)

"Momiji Road" is an area where about 60 Momiji are planted along a 150m stream. During the autumn foliage season, the densely growing Momiji and surrounding trees turn red and yellow, creating a fantastic landscape.

The view from the bridge is particularly beautiful, and the scenery is like a tunnel leading to another world. In mid-November, the leaves fall to the ground and the river turns red, creating a more symbolic world.

It's also excellent for photos and is loved as one of Kawaguchiko's most popular photo spots. Illumination is held at night, and you can enjoy a different beauty from the daytime.

## Three highlights of the Kawaguchiko Autumn Festival

### Beautiful coloring of trees centered on Momiji Street and Momiji Road

![Beautiful coloring of trees centered on Momiji Street and Momiji Road](https://res-4.cloudinary.com/dbm1qiew0/image/upload/q_auto/v1/blog-images/kawaguchiko-autumn-festival%40image1--6-.jpg)

Around the main venue's Momiji Street and Momiji Road, 400-500 Momiji are planted. The densely growing Momiji blends with the surrounding trees, creating a beautiful autumn foliage gradation.

The charm of Kawaguchiko's autumn foliage is also that you can see the spectacular view of Mt. Fuji from both of these areas. The world woven by autumn foliage and Mt. Fuji is beautiful, and you can enjoy the scenery unique to autumn.

### Autumn foliage landscape that becomes even more beautiful with nighttime illumination

![Autumn foliage landscape that becomes even more beautiful with nighttime illumination](https://res-5.cloudinary.com/dbm1qiew0/image/upload/q_auto/v1/blog-images/kawaguchiko-autumn-festival%40image1--2-.jpg)

After sunset, illumination is installed along Momiji Road and Momiji Street, and the venue is wrapped in a more dramatic scene.

Looking over Momiji Road, a golden fantastic world spreads in the darkness, and walking on Momiji Street, the lively voices of people dye the night lights brighter. The lakeside is usually dark and quiet, but during the event period, it changes into a colorful and gorgeous world.

The scene of leaves dyed in red and yellow being illuminated by light is warm and gives warmth even on chilly nights. You can enjoy different beauty during the day and night, so if you have time, please experience both scenery.

### Many food stalls where you can fully enjoy Yamanashi's exquisite cuisine

> ![Many food stalls where you can fully enjoy Yamanashi's exquisite cuisine](https://res-4.cloudinary.com/dbm1qiew0/image/upload/q_auto/v1/blog-images/kawaguchiko-autumn-festival%40image1--4-b.png)
>
> Source: [Official Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/DBuvCyXyxEf/?img_index=3)

At the Kawaguchiko Autumn Festival, one of the attractions is that you can enjoy local food around Mt. Fuji and gourmet food from local shops.

Food stalls line up around the main venue, and you can enjoy one-hand foods such as potatoes and kebabs, as well as hearty meals such as local foods "Houtou" and "Fujinomiya Yakisoba." The fragrant sauce smell and the sound of grilling meat will surely whet your appetite.

It's chilly Kawaguchiko in November, but warm gourmet foods warm both the body and heart. Why not enjoy autumn foliage with food in hand?

## For those with limited time, join a private car tour from Tokyo that efficiently covers key spots in one day!

![Mt. Fuji Full-day Day Trip Tour from Tokyo with a Private Car & Guide](https://res-4.cloudinary.com/dbm1qiew0/image/upload/q_auto/v1/blog-images/kawaguchiko-autumn-festival%40image1--5-b.png)

Many people planning tourism starting from Tokyo may think "it's difficult to include Mt. Fuji sightseeing in the itinerary." However, Mt. Fuji is close to Tokyo and can be enjoyed even on a day trip. Magical Trip offers private tours that allow you to efficiently visit major tourist spots around Mt. Fuji in one day.

Tours are accompanied by local guides knowledgeable about history and culture. You can fully experience the charm of Mt. Fuji in one day by visiting places like Arakura Fuji Sengen Shrine, where you can view spectacular scenery of Mt. Fuji with autumn foliage, and wasabi farms that are rarely visited on independent trips.

The attractive point is that you can enjoy your journey comfortably with hotel pickup service in the morning from anywhere in the city where you're staying.

<Information>

Meeting point: Shinjuku or hotel pick-up

> ![Oishi Park](https://res-5.cloudinary.com/dbm1qiew0/image/upload/q_auto/v1/blog-images/kawaguchiko-autumn-festival%40image1--1-b.png)
>
> Source: [Home of Fujisan Yamanashi](https://www.yamanashi-kankou.jp/nature/autumn.html)

Oishi Park is a park famous for kochia, located on the north side of Kawaguchiko. As autumn deepens, the green leaves of kochia gradually change from green to red and golden colors. The fluffy and adorable kochia creates a scene as if a flock of sheep were playing in a meadow. The scenery woven by kochia and Mt. Fuji is also beautiful, with outstanding photo opportunities that make you want to post on social media and show everyone.

It's within walking distance from the main venue of the Kawaguchiko Autumn Festival, so I recommend extending your visit while viewing Mt. Fuji from the lakeside.

Best viewing period: Early October to early November

Koyodai is an observation deck in the mountains where you can overlook spectacular views of Mt. Fuji. The view of Mt. Fuji towering over the sea of trees is overwhelming, and especially beautiful scenery spreads during autumn foliage season.

My recommendation is the view from Koyodai Tenbo Resthouse. Mt. Fuji rising in blue melts into the scenery of the sea of trees dyed red with autumn foliage, creating an otherworldly scene. It costs 300 yen, but it's a spectacular view you should definitely see if you visit Koyodai.

A trekking course that can be casually enjoyed in about 2 hours round trip is also maintained, so I recommend enjoying the autumn foliage while forest bathing.

## Why Kawaguchiko Is the Go-To Spot for Japan Fall Foliage

Lake Kawaguchi sits on the north side of Mt. Fuji, and that geography matters. Each of the Five Lakes offers a different view of the mountain, but only Lake Kawaguchi delivers the most complete and symmetrical cone reflected in the water — and in autumn you get maple trees layered in front of it.

The Fuji Five Lakes region — Kawaguchiko, Saiko, Yamanakako, Shojiko and Motosuko — all display fall colours, but **Kawaguchiko has the highest concentration of viewing spots, food stalls and public transport**. It's the easiest base for a first-time visitor to central Japan. Honestly, if it's your first autumn trip to Japan and you want that postcard shot, this is where you go.

![Snow-dusted Mount Fuji rising behind red and gold autumn maple leaves in November](https://selfguidejapan.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fimages.selfguidejapan.com%2Fblog%2Fautumn-in-japan-2026-fuji.jpg&w=3840&q=75)Snow-capped Fuji behind fiery maples — the contrast most photographers chase, at its best in mid-November.

## When Do Autumn Leaves Peak at Mt Fuji?

Peak dates shift year to year — warm autumns push everything a week later; cold snaps pull it earlier. Here's how the season typically unfolds around the lake:

#### 🍂 Kawaguchiko foliage, week by week

| Window | What to expect |
| --- | --- |
| Early–mid October | Too early. Lakeside maples are still green; only higher elevations start to turn. |
| Late October | First blushes, especially at elevation. Fewer crowds, but colours aren't at full strength. |
| Early–mid November | **The sweet spot.** North-shore maples turn vibrant and Fuji is often snow-capped. |
| Late November | Still gorgeous — more scattered, fallen leaves, a more symbolic mood. |
| Early December | Winding down. Some late colour in sheltered spots, but the festival has ended. |

💡 Check Japanese foliage maps and recent visitor reports in late October 2026 to fine-tune your dates.

## Kawaguchiko Autumn Leaves 2026: Festival Dates and Details

The Fujikawaguchiko Momiji Festival is the main event. Based on recent years' patterns, the town has confirmed it for **November 7–29, 2026**, featuring the maple corridors, night illuminations, Fuji views and local food stalls. Always confirm the official dates on the Fujikawaguchiko tourism site before locking in accommodation.

### Momiji Corridor: The Main Venue

The festival centres on the **Momiji Corridor (Momiji Kairo)** — a 150-metre stream lined with around 60 maples, with photo angles from the small bridge that crosses the canal. Across the main venue's Momiji Street and Momiji Road, some **400–500 maples** grow densely, blending with the surrounding trees into a beautiful autumn gradation.

### Night Illuminations

The festival's night illuminations are worth planning around. They're held daily at the Maple Corridor from **sunset until 9:00 p.m.** After dark, the red maples take on a completely different mood — warmer, more theatrical.

### Food Stalls and Atmosphere

The main venue gets busy for a reason. Stalls line up around the corridor with one-hand foods like grilled potatoes and kebabs, plus hearty local dishes — **Hoto** (thick wheat noodles in a miso-and-pumpkin stew) and Fujinomiya yakisoba. Perfect for a chilly November evening.

## How to Get to Kawaguchiko From Tokyo

#### 🚆 Tokyo → Kawaguchiko at a glance

| Option | Time | One-way fare | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Highway bus (Shinjuku) | ~2 hrs | ¥2,200 (¥2,000 online) | Cheapest & most direct; ~2 buses/hr. Book ahead in November. |
| Train via Otsuki | ~2.5 hrs | from ¥2,580 | JR Chuo Line to Otsuki, then Fujikyu Railway (¥1,170). One transfer. |
| Direct limited express | ~2 hrs | ¥4,200 | A few per day, seat reservations mandatory. |

💡 The Fujikyu Railway leg is **not** covered by the JR Pass. Bus travel times can stretch during autumn foliage season due to expressway traffic.

For the full transport rundown — every bus and train option, the Kawaguchiko sightseeing bus lines and a two-day plan — see [how to get to Kawaguchiko from Tokyo](https://selfguidejapan.com/blog/kawaguchiko-mount-fuji).

For most self-guided travellers, **the bus wins on price and simplicity**. The train wins if you have a JR Pass covering the Chuo Line portion and don't mind the transfer at Otsuki Station. Book Shinjuku–Kawaguchiko tickets online in advance — seats fill fast on November weekends.

## Getting Around Once You Arrive

Kawaguchiko is spread out. You can walk between the good spots, but you'll waste hours — use the sightseeing buses instead.

### The Sightseeing Buses (Red, Green, Blue Lines)

Three Omni bus lines start from Kawaguchiko Station: the **red Kawaguchiko Line** (every 15 min) runs the eastern and northern shores; the green Saiko Line (every 30 min) covers the southern shore and Lake Saiko; the blue Narusawa–Shojiko–Motosuko Line (every 1–2 hrs) serves the western lakes. The **red line is the one you'll use most** for autumn leaves — it hits Oishi Park and stops within reach of the Momiji Corridor.

### The Bus Pass

The **Kawaguchiko–Saiko–Motosuko Bus Pass** (1-day ¥1,500; 2-day ¥2,000) is valid on all three Omni lines and other regular buses across the lakes. Buy it at Kawaguchiko Station, or the 1-day pass on board. If you're doing more than three rides, the pass pays for itself.

### A Word on Crowds

Autumn weekends are brutal. The buses get so packed that you sometimes can't board and end up waiting a long time. **Go on a weekday if you can. If you can't, start early.**

## Top Autumn Foliage Spots Around Lake Kawaguchi

### Momiji Corridor (Maple Corridor)

The main venue for the Kawaguchiko festival, and the photo you probably came for — covered in detail above.

### Oishi Park

On the north shore, the last stop on the red-line bus, with an open view of Mt. Fuji across the lake. From here you get both Lake Kawaguchi and the mountain in one frame — that magnificent landscape shot with autumn colours in the foreground and Fuji behind.

![Autumn maple leaves framing Mount Fuji across Lake Kawaguchi in November](https://selfguidejapan.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fimages.selfguidejapan.com%2Fblog%2Ftokyo-autumn-leaves-2026-kawaguchiko.jpg&w=3840&q=75)Lake Kawaguchi's north shore — best for the mirror-reflection shot early on a clear November morning.

### Momiji Tunnel

A famous photo spot about 15 minutes by car from the festival venue — a stretch of road canopied by maple trees. Gorgeous, but cramped with photographers on peak weekends.

### Koyodai Observation Deck

For a wider view of the sea of trees around Fuji, head up to Koyodai. Its best viewing period is **early October to early November** — a little earlier than the lakeshore, so it's a good option if you arrive in late October.

### Chureito Pagoda (Fujiyoshida City)

Not directly on Lake Kawaguchi, but close. Famous for Fuji framed with cherry trees in spring — and in autumn those same cherry trees turn copper-red, adding to the maple colour. A classic add-on if you have a third day.

### Mt. Fuji Panoramic Ropeway

A bird's-eye view of the lake and fall colours from an observation deck above the shore. Easy to reach on foot from Kawaguchiko Station or by red-line bus.

## Building a Real Itinerary: 2 Days in Kawaguchiko

This assumes you stay overnight — which you should. Day-trippers miss the illuminations and the early-morning Fuji view.

#### 🗓️ Two days, paced for the light

| When | What you're doing |
| --- | --- |
| Day 1 — midday | Highway bus from Shinjuku, arrive around lunch, drop bags at your ryokan (many have onsen). |
| Day 1 — afternoon | Red-line bus to Oishi Park; walk the north-shore promenade. |
| Day 1 — evening | Momiji Corridor for hoto or yakisoba, then stay for the night illuminations. |
| Day 2 — early AM | **The move:** 6–7 a.m. lakeshore for the mirror-reflection Fuji shot before clouds roll in. |
| Day 2 — late AM | Ride the ropeway to the observation deck, lunch, then bus back to Tokyo. |

💡 With a third day, add Chureito Pagoda in Fujiyoshida or loop down to Lake Saiko for fewer crowds.

## Common Mistakes to Avoid

- **Going on a weekend.** Weekends during the festival are packed, and buses fill beyond capacity. Weekdays are far smoother.
- **Not checking foliage forecasts.** Peak dates shift year to year. Check Japanese weather-service foliage maps and recent visitor reports in late October.
- **Assuming you can see Fuji anytime.** Fuji hides behind clouds a lot; mornings are your best shot. Build in flexibility so you get a second attempt if day one is cloudy.
- **Skipping the bus pass.** If you're hitting more than two spots, buy it at Kawaguchiko Station the moment you arrive.
- **Underestimating the cold.** November averages ~7°C (highs ~13°C, lows near 1°C), and it's colder by the lake at night during illuminations. Bring layers.

## Autumn vs Other Seasons at Mount Fuji

- **Spring (cherry trees):** beautiful but brief; Chureito Pagoda with blossoms is iconic, but no red maples or reliable snow cap.
- **Summer:** green everywhere and hiking season on Fuji itself, but hazier views and often a bare, snowless peak.
- **Autumn foliage:** peak colours _plus_ a snow-capped Fuji — the visual feast most photographers want.
- **Winter:** crisp air and the best Fuji visibility, but no foliage. Hot springs feel extra good.

Autumn hits the sweet spot for scenery lovers — which is exactly why the Fuji area gets so busy from October to mid-November. Our [autumn in Japan 2026](https://selfguidejapan.com/blog/autumn-in-japan-2026) guide has the wider seasonal picture, and [Japan in November 2026](https://selfguidejapan.com/blog/japan-in-november-2026) covers the month in detail.

## Turning This Into Your Wider Japan Trip

Japan's fall foliage rolls south from northern Hokkaido starting in September, sweeps through the Japanese Alps in October, then hits central Japan and Tokyo in November. If Kawaguchiko is your anchor, sequence the rest north-to-south to chase the colour wave:

1. **Fly into Tokyo** (Haneda or Narita); spend two or three days.
2. **Head to Kawaguchiko for two nights**, hitting peak foliage on a weekday.
3. **Continue to Hakone or Kyoto** — both extend the fall-colour experience with different scenery.
4. **Return via Tokyo** for late-November foliage in the city parks — see our [Tokyo autumn leaves 2026](https://selfguidejapan.com/blog/tokyo-autumn-leaves-2026) guide.

Self-guiding this route is very doable. What you need is a solid rail-and-bus plan, booked accommodation, and a rough day-by-day sketch that leaves room for weather. That's exactly what we build.

## FAQ: Mount Fuji Autumn Leaves 2026

When exactly will autumn leaves peak at Kawaguchiko in 2026?expand\_more

Most years, peak colour lands in mid-November around Lake Kawaguchi. Check foliage forecasts in mid-October 2026 to refine your dates, since warm autumns push the peak later.

Is the Kawaguchiko Momiji Festival free?expand\_more

Yes. Entry to the main venue and the illuminations is free. You only pay for food, drinks, and any museums or attractions you enter.

Can I do it as a day trip from Tokyo?expand\_more

Technically yes, but you'll miss the illuminations and the sunrise Fuji view. Even one overnight makes a big difference.

Do I need a car?expand\_more

No. The red-line sightseeing bus covers the main spots. A car helps for the Momiji Tunnel or exploring beyond Kawaguchiko, but it's not required.

What if it's cloudy and I can't see Fuji?expand\_more

The foliage is still beautiful on its own. Try again the next morning — clouds often clear by 6–7 a.m. One more reason to stay overnight.

Are the buses hard to catch during the festival?expand\_more

On weekends, yes — expect delays, though extra buses are often added on the red line. Weekdays are much smoother.

Is Kawaguchiko good for hot springs?expand\_more

Yes. Many ryokan and hotels around the lake have onsen baths, some with Fuji views from the tub — exactly what you want after a cold day chasing colour.

Timing Fuji is one thing. Building a working itinerary with trains, the right bus pass, a lakeside ryokan and backup days for cloud cover is another. Visit autumn leaves spots in Tokyo](https://media-cdn.tripadvisor.com/media/attractions-splice-spp-360x240/14/66/d5/12.jpg)\\ \\ Red, Yellow and Brown - Visit autumn leaves spots in Tokyo\\ \\ ¥29,800\\ \\ ![Viator](https://japantravel.navitime.com/static/parche/20260828-2/images/common/provider/affiliate/leisure/80013.svg)](https://www.viator.com/tours/Tokyo/Red-Yellow-Brown-Visit-famous-autumn-leaves-spots-in-Tokyo/d334-485648P2?mcid=42383&pid=P00101298&pid=P00101298&mcid=42383&medium=link&campaign=autumn) ## Best Autumn Locations - [![Lake Kawaguchi Shore (Autumn Leaves Corridor)](https://data-dev.pcstrg.cld.navitime.jp/event/momiji/90011_al00102_01.jpg)](https://japantravel.navitime.com/en/area/jp/spot/90011-al00102/) [Lake Kawaguchi Shore (Autumn Leaves Corridor)](https://japantravel.navitime.com/en/area/jp/spot/90011-al00102/) Yamanashi Minamitsuru-gun Fujikawaguchikomachi KawaguchiBest SeasonMid-November to late NovemberCurrent StatusーDuring the autumn foliage season, about 60 old maple trees on both sides of the river turn bright red, creating a corridor of red leaves. The Kawaguchiko Lakeside (Autumn Foliage Corridor) is a popular autumn foliage spot. From early to late November, when the leaves are at their best, there is also a light-up event, allowing visitors to enjoy an even more fantastic world. At the same time, the Fuji Kawaguchiko Autumn Leaves Festival is held. - [![Meijijingu Gaien](https://data-dev.pcstrg.cld.navitime.jp/event/momiji/90011_al00077_01.jpg)](https://japantravel.navitime.com/en/area/jp/spot/90011-al00077/) [Meijijingu Gaien](https://japantravel.navitime.com/en/area/jp/spot/90011-al00077/) Tokyo Shinjuku-kuBest SeasonMid-November - Early DecemberCurrent StatusーMeiji Jingu Gaien, rich in historic sites and famous trees, is especially known for the four-row street trees Ginkgo Avenue from Aoyama Street entrance to the Gaien Central Square circular road, loved throughout the seasons. The Jingu Gaien Ginkgo Festival held from mid-November to early December has become an autumn tradition in the city center. - [![Jozankei](https://data-dev.pcstrg.cld.navitime.jp/event/momiji/90011_al00068_01.jpg)](https://japantravel.navitime.com/en/area/jp/spot/90011-al00068/) [Jozankei](https://japantravel.navitime.com/en/area/jp/spot/90011-al00068/) Hokkaido Sapporo-shi Minami-ku Jozankeionsennishi 4-chome (Futami ParkBest SeasonEarly October to mid-OctoberCurrent StatusーWhen it comes to autumn leaves in Sapporo, Jozankei is famous. We recommend sightseeing on the Autumn Leaves Kappa Bus which operates for about 20 days from early October, the best viewing season. For about one hour, a local guide will show you the highlights of the autumn leaves. Nishiki Bridge and Shigure Bridge over Maizuru's rapids and Shirai River are especially beautiful. - [![Kiyomizudera Temple](https://data-dev.pcstrg.cld.navitime.jp/event/momiji/90011_al00005_01.jpg)](https://japantravel.navitime.com/en/area/jp/spot/90011-al00005/) [Kiyomizudera Temple](https://japantravel.navitime.com/en/area/jp/spot/90011-al00005/) Kyoto Kyoto-shi Higashiyama-ku Kiyomizu 1-294Best SeasonLate November to early DecemberCurrent StatusーA temple located in Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto City, it is one of the most popular spots in Japan where you can enjoy spectacular views of cherry blossoms, fresh greenery, and autumn leaves throughout the four seasons. From the main hall, you can overlook mountains dyed entirely red, and from the inner sanctuary, you can enjoy the contrast between the cliff-protruding Kiyomizu Stage and the autumn leaves. At night, the temple is illuminated, allowing you to enjoy a magical beauty different from daytime. - [![Chuzenji Lake](https://data-dev.pcstrg.cld.navitime.jp/event/momiji/90011_al00052_01.jpg)](https://japantravel.navitime.com/en/area/jp/spot/90011-al00052/) [Chuzenji Lake](https://japantravel.navitime.com/en/area/jp/spot/90011-al00052/) Tochigi Nikko-shi ChugushiBest SeasonMid-October to early NovemberCurrent StatusーAbout 20,000 years ago, the lava from the eruption of Mount Nantai dammed the valley, forming the original shape of Lake Chuzenji, located at the entrance of Oku-Nikko. Known as a scenic spot with beautiful azaleas in early summer and autumn foliage in fall. Taking a sightseeing boat to enjoy the view from the water is also exceptional, and during the autumn foliage season, a Momiji Meguri Course is operated. - [![Special Place of Scenic Beauty Kenrokuen](https://data-dev.pcstrg.cld.navitime.jp/event/momiji/90011_al00048_01.jpg)](https://japantravel.navitime.com/en/area/jp/spot/90011-al00048/) [Special Place of Scenic Beauty Kenrokuen](https://japantravel.navitime.com/en/area/jp/spot/90011-al00048/) Ishikawa Kanazawa-shi Kenrokumachi 1Best SeasonEarly November to early DecemberCurrent StatusーReflecting the culture of Kaga Hyakumangoku, the historical cultural heritage and one of Japan's three great gardens, the stroll-style garden Special Place of Scenic Beauty Kenrokuen is planted with many momiji, sakura, and keyaki on Yamazaki Mountain and Horai Island in Kasumigaike Pond. You can enjoy the magnificent scenery during the autumn leaves season from mid-November to early December. - [![Arashiyama](https://data-dev.pcstrg.cld.navitime.jp/event/momiji/90011_al00085_01.jpg)](https://japantravel.navitime.com/en/area/jp/spot/90011-al00085/) [Arashiyama](https://japantravel.navitime.com/en/area/jp/spot/90011-al00085/) Kyoto Kyoto-shi Ukyo-ku Saga Nishikyo-ku ArashiyamaBest SeasonLate November to early DecemberCurrent StatusーArashiyama, a nationally designated historic site and scenic spot, has long been famous as a picturesque location and is also known as a famous spot for cherry blossoms in spring and autumn leaves in fall. The autumn leaves reflected on the surface of the Katsura River and Togetsukyo Bridge are elegant, and it is no wonder that poets have composed verses about it. After the Momiji Festival held on the second Sunday of November, light-ups are held from mid-November to early December. - [![Hakone Gora Park](https://data-dev.pcstrg.cld.navitime.jp/event/momiji/90011_al00058_01.jpg)](https://japantravel.navitime.com/en/area/jp/spot/90011-al00058/) [Hakone Gora Park](https://japantravel.navitime.com/en/area/jp/spot/90011-al00058/) Kanagawa Ashigarashimo-gun Hakonemachi Gora 1300Best SeasonEarly November to late NovemberCurrent StatusーHakone Gora Park, where various flowers bloom throughout the seasons and visitors can enjoy a historic tea house, café, and craft experience house in many ways, is very popular for enjoying autumn leaves along with the autumn roses in the rose garden. The autumn leaves around the fountain and the view from the Hakuundō Tea House are also very charming. - [![Miyajima (Momijidani Park)](https://data-dev.pcstrg.cld.navitime.jp/event/momiji/90011_al00106_01.jpg)](https://japantravel.navitime.com/en/area/jp/spot/90011-al00106/) [Miyajima (Momijidani Park)](https://japantravel.navitime.com/en/area/jp/spot/90011-al00106/) Hiroshima Hatsukaichi-shi MiyajimachoBest SeasonMid-November to late NovemberCurrent StatusーA scenic spot selected as one of Japan's Three Views in the Nihon Kokujiko by the Edo period Confucian scholar Hayashi Shunsai. Among them, Momijidani Park at the foot of the Misen primeval forest is renowned as the best spot in Miyajima. Momijidani Park has about 700 maple trees including Iroha maple, big maple, urihada maple, and yamamomiji. In mid to late November, the entire area turns a fiery red during the autumn leaves season. The quiet flow of the Momijidani River running through the park combined with the scenic beauty of Misen creates an atmosphere as if you are enjoying autumn leaves hunting in a mountain valley, which is highly praised. ## Related Articles - [【2025 Japan Autumn Foliage Guide】5 Must-See Koyo Spots: Recommendations for Kyoto's Tofuku-ji, Kiyomizu-dera, Arashiyama, Mt. # Autumn Leaves Forecast 2025

Discover Japan during the beautiful season of autumn leaves
Toyama

Surrounded by rich nature, Japan has four magical seasons. Autumn is considered one of the most beautiful as the landscape turns vibrant shades of orange, yellow, and red. Colorful autumn leaves, known as koyo, have been admired in Japan for centuries and today, together with the Sakura (cherry blossoms), attract a large number of visitors, both local and international. The perfect time to visit these incredible sights is from late September to early December, depending on the place, elevation, and temperature of the year

Each year, the season of scenic autumn leaves begins in colder areas of northern Hokkaido and gradually moves southward to central and southern Japan. In each region, the mountains are colored first, then scenes of colored leaves spread into city gardens, parks, and temples. Both areas are definitely worth a visit.

The secret behind the picturesque vivid foliage lies in Japan’s typical autumn weather – a difference in temperature between cooler mornings, warm sunny daytime, and cold evenings that allow autumn leaves to change.

The scenic autumn season is the time of year when it is neither too hot nor too cold, making it easy and comfortable to travel. This is also the season of harvest and fine seasonal food, which potentially makes autumn the best time for you to visit.

# Mt. Fuji in Peak Autumn: Kawaguchiko

When is the best time to see autumn leaves with Mount Fuji, and what are the best places to go to?

![Ariel Land](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/fw5u8ou1/production/91c8b8e50e259fef77f10c3fb1063508c5d7e993-4608x3456.jpg?rect=396,0,4212,3456&w=3840&q=80&fit=clip&auto=format)

This is my 4th time in Kawaguchiko, prior times being in summer and winter. I'm so glad that I'm finally able to see Fuji surrounded by leaves bursting in colors of red, orange, and yellow. Fuji will always be such a classic, but autumn leaves definitely make everything more magical.

### When is the best time to go?

Mid November is usually close to peak foliage, in last year's case I went on Nov 16, 2021 and everything was as bright as it can be. If you are traveling internationally then you can aim for **mid-late November**.

[**2025 Kawaguchiko Autumn Festival**](https://fujisan.ne.jp/en/pages/433/) is from **11/1 ~ 11/30**. Night time light up is sunset till 9:30pm. It's free to visit and there are food and drink stalls around it.

To check more accurately closer to the date, these two webpages gives you live update of foliage by region. There are simple icons with leaves in green, yellow, red, brown to indicate the status of the foliage.

1\. [https://tenki.jp/lite/kouyou/](https://www.blogger.com/blog/post/edit/8124579507526577941/7017981506019016464#)

2\. [https://weathernews.jp/s/koyo/](https://www.blogger.com/blog/post/edit/8124579507526577941/7017981506019016464#) (this allows you to filter everything that is currently in peak foliage)

### Getting to Kawaguchiko

There are several ways of getting there and each have their own advantage:

- **By Car:**

It's about a 1hr 20min drive without traffic from Shinjuku to Kawaguchiko. The advantage is you can get around the different sites at Kawaguchiko faster, the disadvantage though is that it is subject to traffic and parking costs. With bad weekend traffic, the one way drive can take over 3hrs, and during peak foliage season the parking can cost as much as ¥1,000 per location.
- **By Train:** The Fuji Excursion is a 1hr 50min train ride from Shinjuku to Kawaguchiko Station. It runs twice on weekdays and 3 times on weekends. The best part is the train is direct and there's no traffic so you'll always be on time. After getting to Kawaguchiko area though you still need to take busses to get around the lake. Or you can choose to rent bikes and ride around the lake. The one disadvantage is that this route is more expensive, around ¥4,130 one way. There are 2 sections of the route, Shinjuku to Otsuki and Otsuki to Kawaguchiko. The first is covered by the JR rail pass however the second part is not and it's almost always fully booked so you can't go on without a reserved seat ticket.
- **By Highway bus:** If you take the express bus from Shinjuku station, it will take you to Kawaguchiko in 1hr45min and it costs less than ¥4,000 round trip so it is half the price of the train. There's also multiple departures and returns a day so this is flexible on the schedule. One disadvantage though is that it will be subject to traffic. On weekends it can be up to 3hrs one way. When I returned to Tokyo on a 3pm bus, it was delayed by about 20mins due to rush hour traffic in the city. You can book the tickets online in English [**here**](https://www.blogger.com/blog/post/edit/8124579507526577941/7017981506019016464#).

If you'd like to read more about the trains since it can get complicated, here's a detailed article: [https://gowithguide.com/blog/how-to-book-fuji-excursion-4138](https://www.blogger.com/blog/post/edit/8124579507526577941/7017981506019016464#)

### Getting around Kawaguchiko

After arriving in Kawaguchiko, if not driving then the most common way to get around is with the Kawaguchiko Sightseeing Bus (Red Bus). You'll be able to see all the major autumn foliage spots by only using the red bus and some walking.

If you'd like to see Lake Saiko or Lake Shojiko, you can use the Green and Blue Busses. All bus details can be found [**here**](https://www.blogger.com/blog/post/edit/8124579507526577941/7017981506019016464#).

### Major Spots to See Autumn Foliage

There are quite a few spots that are reachable by public transport where you can admire Mt.Fuji and beautiful Japanese maple or other autumn foliage such as ginkgo trees. If you are driving, please note that parking is ¥1,000 for each spot during the Autumn Festival period.

### Oishi Park

This park on the north shore of Lake Kawaguchi is known for its flowers. There's tulips, pink moss, lupins, and weeping cherry blossoms in spring; lavender, hydrangeas, and daisies in summer; Japanese maple, ginkgo, and kokia plants in autumn. It's a place where you can always go see flowers and I would recommend to put towards the top of your list of places to go to in the area. There's also a little gift shop which sell snacks and drinks as well.

![Ariel Land](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/fw5u8ou1/production/772a13ef3605ccffc11964cad2fda3db61355648-432x324.jpg?w=3840&q=80&fit=clip&auto=format)

Image from Mt Fuji taken at Oishi Park

### Momiji Tunnel

(not to be confused with Maple Corridor)

This tunnel is actually a road for cars to drive on and is further west from Oishi park. You have to walk there as there's no public transport, but it is more quiet because of that. Walk down towards the lake front to find more beautiful trees lined on the shores.

![Ariel Land](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/fw5u8ou1/production/cb772f7ec3da20f302a7e228a3a086ce92cdea9c-240x320.jpg?w=3840&q=80&fit=clip&auto=format)

### Mt. Fuji Panoramic Ropeway

This ropeway takes you up to Kawaguchiko Tenjozan Park which gives you an incredible view of Mt. Fuji. You can actually take the ropeway up and hike down which only takes about 40mins. There's also two swings, however you need to pay ¥500 to use it. Fuji is directly in front of the swings but it was covered by clouds when I went.

Still, the bunny shrine on top with Maple shaped Ema (wooden wish plaques) is really cute to visit. There's also a bell of love you can ring to bring luck to romance.

![Ariel Land](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/fw5u8ou1/production/574c1b7186ed0a6ebda61869aae7a0b1a5baf1a5-481x361.jpg?w=3840&q=80&fit=clip&auto=format)

### Kawaguchiko Station

Lastly, there's a free foot bath at Kawaguchiko Station which is free from 10am-3pm. It's perfect after walking around for a while in the autumn breeze.

🍁 Experience the beauty of red maple leaves at the Kawaguchiko Maple Corridor

The autumn foliage season is approaching, so get ready to check in at the Maple Corridor in Japan 🇯🇵.

This spot is considered one of the most beautiful places to view autumn leaves. If you visit Lake Kawaguchiko in late November, you’re guaranteed to witness the vibrant colors 🍁😍.

At the Maple Corridor, both sides of the path are lined with maple trees that change their leaves to shades of red, orange, and yellow. The fallen leaves cover the water surface of the canal like a carpet, making it a highlight of any trip to Lake Kawaguchiko.

At night, the area is illuminated, and the red maple leaves contrast beautifully with the lights. It’s highly recommended to visit again in the evening for a different, magical atmosphere with fewer crowds.

If you have any tips or know of great photo spots at the Maple Corridor, feel free to share 😊.

Taking advantage of the Lake Kawaguchi Autumn Leaves Corridor Festival currently underway, I went to see the autumn leaves of Mount Fuji.
